You finally gather up all your dirty clothes, separate the colors, and get ready to throw everything in, only to find a cat sitting inside the drum like they've been waiting for you to arrive. Judging by the look on their face, they're not particularly interested in giving up their spot.
Apparently, the washing machine is prime feline real estate.
Cats have always been drawn to strange little hiding places, especially ones that weren't designed with them in mind. Cardboard boxes, bathroom sinks, kitchen cabinets, and laundry baskets are all popular choices. Two kittens are better than one, especially when they're already best friends. You get twice the cuteness, twice the mischief, and twice the number of cats trying to steal your dinner. Your house might become a little more chaotic, but at least the kittens have someone else to bother when you're trying to sleep.
Bonded cats have their own little world, and we're just lucky enough to watch it. They'll spend hours chasing each other around the house, fighting over the same toy, and squeezing into beds that are clearly meant for one cat. Five minutes after a dramatic wrestling match, you'll find them curled up together like nothing happened.
We love seeing kittens grow up alongside their siblings. They learn how to play together, keep each other company, and develop little routines that their…

As someone who recently got married (thank you, you may send gifts in the form of cat pics), I currently have a lot to say about weddings. I didn't think I would be one of those bridezillas, but the stress leading up to the wedding really did a number on me. Organizing a hundred people coming from all over the world to get to one place, on time, is much harder than it sounds. Let alone making sure everyone has enough to eat, and especially drink. I will say that it was one of the best nights of my life, but I'm so glad it's over and I never want to repeat it again.
You have no idea how many things can go wrong on your wedding day. For example, unforeseen gale winds blowing over your decorati…

articles.description:
"Man's nest friend" is apparently a saying that applies to big cats too. 
Everyone knows that dogs are so ridiculously friendly. It's one of the things that they are the most known for, actually. Man's best friend. Of course, as cat people, we think that this is slightly discriminatory against cats, who are our purrsonal best friends. But alas, we accept it. Because it's accurate. Because dogs have the ability to befriend literally anything that moves. Dogs will become best friends with ducks, with rabbits, with chicks, with foxes, with parrots… Basically every animal that you can think of, a dog has likely befriended in the past. 
Even cats, who are so, so different than dogs - in their behavior, in their interpretations of other creatures' behaviors - cannot withstand canine cuteness. Ca…
articles.title: Tiny lion cub who was abandoned by his mother gets paired up with the sweetest Labrador foster mom, and the two become instant best friends: 'She looked at [the cub] and didn't see a lion, she saw one of hers'

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
When a cat chooses you, they will not stop at anything until you choose them back. 
Usually, when we talk about cat adoption stories, it's always so easy and wholesome. A cat chooses its human, and the human simply has no choice in the matter. Right? And that really is how it is most times. Cats are very purrsistent once they decide that they want to adopt someone, and we - usually - can't resist them for long. Of course, it's not always easy. It's not always that cut and dry. Sometimes, you really are not ready to adopt a cat. Sometimes, you have too many of them. And sometimes, the cat who chose you… already technically belongs to someone else. 
At what point is caving into a cat's demands considered stealing them? Because the cat in today's story clearly made a decision. We don't know much about how he is treated at home. All that we know is that for two years, this cat has been sneaking into the neighbor's home, demanding cuddles and love at every opportunity. Now, maybe he's genuinely loved at home. Maybe it's all fine there. That doesn't take away from the fact that this adorably unique cat chose a human. And although that human managed to resist for much longer than we would have, eventually, like anyone who's been chosen by a cat before, that human caved.
articles.title: Neighbor's unique Devon Rex cat spends 2 years breaking into person's home, demanding cuddles; they finally cave, and now, the cat has 2 forever homes

articles.author: Giuliana Tiscioni
articles.description:
What's a thing all cats love to do? Climb onto anything belonging to their hoomans and claim it as their own. 
If I had a dollar for every single time my cat has jumped over my dining room chairs, my table, my kitchen countertops, my couch, or my bed, I'm telling you, I would retire tomorrow without having to ever work a single day in my life ever again. And I'm betting that is the case for many, if not all, of you out there, cat pawrents. 
At this point, my chairs have become my cat's property. She sleeps there all the time, and the pillows are covered in her fur. I'm just grateful that she learned not to sharpen her claws on those chairs; otherwise, I would have to replace them in a week, and they're made of solid wood. They're not exactly cheap. She has a specific place to sharpen her claws, and though it took some time for her to scratch random pieces of furniture, eventually she learned to scratch in a specific place without ruining anything. Kudos to my furball for understanding instructions. 
The thing with cats is that they believe everything belongs to them: chairs, pillows, couches, clothes, the house, or whatever, and they will never hesitate to claim those things by sitting on top of them. Here's a collection of cat photos of cats that picked a spot and sat there to rule the world from a comfortable chair.
articles.title: 26 Purrfect Cats Ruling Over the World From Their Hooman's Chairs and Couches

articles.author: Cata Holmes
articles.description:
Who needs a yoga mat when you've got a cardboard box, and you're a cat?
Have you ever seen how a cat can shape-shift and squeeze into the tiniest space? Honestly, it's an amazing thing to see. I really cannot understand how they can flex their bones and their whole body just to squeeze through a tiny hole in the wall or fit into the smallest box in the house. How can they find that comfortable? Also, did you know there's no scientific name for that ability? Who would have thought! I don't know of any other animal on Earth with such a gift, and I find it crazy that no one has decided to name it. Well, not the scientists, at least. Because the internet world decided to call that "Liquid cats", and it fits perfectly. 
Although no scientist has given this cat feature a nerdier name, one did study it to understand how cats think when they try to fit into small spaces. A 2024 study called "Cats are (almost) liquid" examined exactly this: how they squeeze into narrow spaces and adjust their bodies to fit, no matter how small or uncomfortable it might be. 
This ability really amazes me, and I'm intrigued to understand why they do it. Maybe there's no reason, and they like to flex their bodies… maybe they find it relaxing. That's why I find it funny to compare it to pet Pilates. If you think about it, one leg squeezing the other, sucking in the belly, twisting and turning, it sounds like a stretching class or a Pilates session. So, perhaps cats are working out when doing this! And kudos to them! Just looking at them motivates me to get my work out in!
articles.title: These Cats in Boxes Are Taking Pet Pilates to a Whole New Level With Their Purrfectly Flexible Poses

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
The Cat Distribution System has some suspiciously good timing. You can spend months thinking about getting another cat, making plans, and convincing yourself that you'll wait until the time is right. Meanwhile, some lucky humans casually mention wanting a kitten over dinner and find one waiting outside their house a few hours later.
We're starting to suspect the neighborhood cats are listening to our conversations.
Cat lovers know how dangerous it is to start thinking about fostering. You tell yourself you're only going to help a few kittens find homes, but suddenly you're imagining tiny paws running across the floor and little furballs sleeping on your chest. You've already picked out names, researched kitten food, and mentally rearranged your furniture to accommodate a cat tree.
The actu…
articles.title: Woman wishes for a kitten over dinner and comes home to discover the Cat Distribution System was listening

articles.author: Laurent Shinar
articles.description:
Look, it is a sad fact of the feline pawrenting world but one that all cat pawrents have to come to terms with. Unless you had the good fortune of knowing your cat before you adopted them, there is little way of knowing whether they will turn into cuddly cuties or touchless  terrors. It is simply the luck of the draw, even though many feline fans will try to tell you that certain kinds of cats are cuddlier than others. But from our deep nad expansive knowledge, we know that the only truth there is out there is that you never truly know what you are in for when adopting a cat. This has left more than a few of us cat obsessed hoomans with felines who are touchless terrors. The kind of cat that if you even look at them with the intention of wanting to touch, pet or worst of all cuddle them, they will run for the hills. Well, more likely their hardest to reach hiding place.
And as you can imagine if you are lucky enough not to be included in this category of pawrent it is not a fun place to be. All those lonely nights you hoped would be filled with the warmth of your cat's love. All those quiet mornings you hoped to spend sunbathing alongside your feline on the back porch. All those dreams are scattered like litter all over the floor. But there is still something that can be done to make up for that kind of misery and that is indulging in a wholesome collection of soul warming cattos like this one to give you the deep-seated emotions of satiation that only that kind of deep and vulnerable feline love can give a person.
And with that we leave you to dive into this delightful deluge of cat children and hope that they are able to fill the hole in your heart as best as they can. As is often the case with cats it might take them a second to find it and assimilate, but the second they do they can fill any size or shape of hole, especially an emotional one. So know that you are in good hands.
articles.title: 24 Soul Warming Memes fur Pawrents Whose Cat Child Refuses to Cuddle them

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Babe, wake up, new cat just dropped. 
Here, at ICHC, we pride ourselves on being cat expurrts. All of us writers have been here for years at this point. There is not a single piece of internet cat news that we have missed. The new cat breed that was discovered? We were on that. There is not a single cat meme that has evaded us. Heck, some of our own handmade memes have gotten attention online. Every cat vet emergency is something that we've seen before. Except when it comes to our cats, who make us panic when they do anything slightly off. 
We know cats. Exept that apparently, we don't know them well enough. Somehow, after years of working in the cat field, today, we were caught off guard. We thought we had seen all the unique and rare cats that existed already. The Maine Coons, the Cornish Rex, the common orange… because oranges are all special in their own ways. But we were wrong. And we're so happy about that. A new cat discovered is always something to celebrate. And if that cat is a hilarious, chaotic menace… then all the better. 
At 11 years of age, this cat's owners, unfortunately, could no longer give him the attention that he needed, so they started looking for other options. Of course, rehoming a cat is always difficult, but they managed to find the purrfect home for him. It's going to take him a while to get used to all the new things, but he knows he's safe and that he is loved. And that's what matters. Also, he is uniquely adorable. Scroll. You'll see what we mean.
articles.title: 'He's twice the size of my other Sphynx cats': Couple adopts an 11-year-old giant Peterbald cat after his owners can no longer care for him, and he fills their house with hilarious chaos

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Our parents always try to give us the best life that they can. This leopard couple succeeded in doing it for their baby. 
I think that this is something that every child can relate to. At some point in our lives, we become aware of our parents' finances. We get a deeper understanding of how they grew up, what their childhood looked like, and all the ways that they tried to make our lives better. We realize which things we took for granted that we shouldn't have. It's a little mind-blowing. Suddenly, we're a lot more thankful for everything that they have given us than we were before - all the ways that they worked so hard to make our lives better. That desire, of course, is true for all parents, not just humans. Felines are the same. 
This desire to make life for our kids better is why stray cats sometimes bring their babies to the humans that they trust. It's why cats co-parent, taking care of babies from different litters together. And we're sure that the leopards in today's story, all 13 who were living in captivity, were trying to make life for their babies better in the same way. They simply couldn't - because of the conditions they lived in. Bad humans are everywhere. But so are good ones. And when the good ones came to rescue these 13 leopards, 2 of them were about to have a baby. 
They lived in captivity, but their cub was born into a life full of love. And that's what all parents want for their babies.
articles.title: Tiny black leopard is born to rescued parents who survived a terrible past, and when his mom can't raise him, humans step in to give him a life full of love

articles.author: Blake Seidel
articles.description:
You can't truly understand what it's like living with cats until you're a cat pawrent yourself. So for all of you cat "owners" out there, we've gathered the weekly top 20 hissterical, heartwarming, and silly tweets that highlight all the cuteness and crime that goes on in our homes daily.
Just like how a childless couple can't compare their lives to the lives of a couple with a hooman kid or two, someone who doesn't own a cat can't compare their lives to the life of a cat pawrent. How can you explain that heartwarming feeling when you open your door to hear the little pitter-patter of paws running to greet you followed by a chorus of happy meows? How can you describe what it's like to wake up in the middle of the night to your cat climbing under the covers to snuggle up next to you? And ho…
articles.title: 20 Heartwarming and Silly Tweets That Perfectly Capture Life With a Cat (October 26, 2026)

articles.author: Blake Seidel
articles.description:
Soon, the clock will go back one hour and we'll be plunged into meowternal darkness (also known as Daylight Savings Time). On top of that, the weather is gloomy and its getting colder. How's a cat lover like you or me supposed to stay pawsitive during these cloudy and dreary conditions? Well - with all the feline funnies the internet has to offer, of course!
In theory, I love gloomy weather. GIve me gray skies, a blanket, a hot cup of coffee, and absolutely nowhere to be, and I am thriving. But when the rain lasts for days, the sun disappears before dinner, and every trip outside feels like a purrmanently wet obstacle course, the coziness starts to wear off into pure annoyance. During this time of the year, I need something small and stoopid to resent my brain, and I mean that in the most loving way pawssible. That stupid thing is a ridiculous cat meme. 
Give me all the dramatic feline faces, pictures of cats sitting somewhere they absolutely should not be, and a plethora of feline funnies. Sometimes, that is enough to pull me out of the weather-induced gloom and remind me that the whole day is not ruined just because the sky looks miserable and my socks are a little wet. Lucky for you, I'm something of a cat meme expurrt as the Managing Editor of I Can Has Cheezburger, so I went and gathered some uplifting funny cat memes for you to battle the gloom and doom with giggles and glee!
articles.title: A Fresh Step of Uplifting Feline Funnies to Fight the Gloomy Weather With Giggles and Glee

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
The CDS works in meowsterious ways. Maybe it even sends us messages from loved ones in the afterlife. 
We always talk about the power of the CDS. How it always finds us in the most unexpected times, in the most unexpected ways. And although we nearly never expect it when a cat adopts us, it always somehow happens at the purrfect time. We may think that we're not ready or that we can't do it, but the cats know better. They believe in us enough, and then, it just kind of… works out. That's how it happened for me, when I adopted my cat. I wasn't expecting it, I didn't think I could do it, and 11 years later, I give advice to new cat owners - in my purrsonal life and here on ICHC. 
Maybe there is a reason for all of this. The CDS really does work in meowsterious ways. In some ways, it feels like the CDS is listening to us. That's why the cats always seem to come at the right time. But maybe it's not only listening to us. Maybe it's listening to everyone, including the ones of us who have crossed the rainbow bridge. At least, this is what the person in today's story has experienced. They are convinced that their late brother sent them on a mission to save some stray kittens in need of help. He loved cats, especially ginger cats, and before he passed, his sister asked him to send her cats. Guess what happened next? Signs. Signs everywhere. Ginger cats all over the place. And then, the biggest sigh, a pile of kittens waiting for her to save them.
articles.title: Woman asks late brother to send her orange cats as signs that he's still around, then finds a pile of kittens in need of help

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
If there is anything that we need today, it's a little peace and quiet. And cat memes. 
Over the past couple of years, with all the chaos and the things and the stuff, all that we have wanted has been some… peace and quiet. Just one day on social media when nothing bad happens. One day when we go on Twitter or Instagram and see nothing but cute pictures of cats. That is all that we have wanted, and we have not gotten it. Nope. Not even one day. The universe has been something else ever since around 2020. But one thing has remained stable. One thing about the internet will never change. That's why people like me keep going on there, keep scrolling through the chaos. We do it because it know that no matter what is happening in the world, cat memes will always reign supreme on the internet. 
Listen, I was doing this way before I got my current job. In fact, when I started writing for ICHC, a part of me was worried that I would get tired of looking at silly cat memes all day long. But that has not happened. It's been the opposite, if anything. I spend all day scrolling through cat content online, all day searching for the positivity in the world, and then, I get to come here and share it with all of you guys, and hopefully, this way, I can send a little bit of peace and quiet your way.
articles.title: 25 Warm and Wholesome Cat Memes to Wrap Your Paws Around a Little Peace and Quiet

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
One cat is great. Two cats are even better. Three cats? Now we're talking. Ask any cat lover how many cats they'd ideally have, and there's a good chance their answer is at least one more than they currently own.
It's hard to be satisfied with just one when there are so many adorable kitties out there waiting to be loved.
Every cat has its own little purrsonality, which is part of the problem. You might already have a cuddly orange boy who follows you everywhere, but that doesn't mean you wouldn't also love a sassy tortie who runs the household. A fluffy little void would be a lovely addition, too. And who could say no to a pair of bonded kittens?
Before long, you've mentally adopted half the cats at your local shelter.
Cat lovers also have a habit of finding potential new family members e…
articles.title: The More The Meowier With These Cat Memes Celebrating Feline-Filled Homes

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
You know you're a cat person when you can't walk past a stray without stopping to say hello. It doesn't matter if you're running late, carrying groceries, or supposed to be somewhere else. If there's a kitty nearby, you're going to spend at least five minutes trying to make friends with them.
Sometimes, those five minutes turn into a whole rescue mission.
We've all heard stories about people going out for groceries and coming home with a cat instead. One minute they're minding their own business, and the next they're buying litter boxes, picking out toys, and trying to figure out how to explain the new family member to everyone at home.
Stray cats have a pretty impressive talent for finding the right humans. Some are cautious and take weeks to warm up to people, while others will march rig…
articles.title: Woman goes to work on her day off and ends up rescuing a sweet dumpster kitty who steals her heart

articles.author: Laurent Shinar
articles.description: Coming across a family of feral kittens in your back yard is no easy thing to deal with, but when one of those kittens presents as a wibbly wobbly kitten who is barely able to cat, well, that is a whole different kettle of fish. And that is how our story begins with the appearance of a momma cat and her two babies, one of which had obvious problems standing up, walking and running. Though it was obvious that the feline's difficulties were not born of injures, it was not clear as to what actually was the cause of its physical difficulties. Initially our fur friendly family kept their distance, solely feeding the tiny felines as and when they came to visit. But soon things would change when the healthy kitten of the two suddenly stopped showing up. This was cause for concern seeing as their …
articles.title: Wobbly kitten spotted struggling to cat in family garden given furever home safe from circling predators

articles.author: Celeste Mello
articles.description:
Do we really need an occasion to wear something that makes us happy?
Whenever I buy new clothes, I start looking for any occasion to wear them. My standards for what counts as an occasion are extremely generous. Going to the movies? Perfect. Going to the supermarket? Also perfect. The cashier clearly didn't ask to see my new outfit, but they're going to. Period.
My friends tease me because I'll buy something and wear it all week. Well, I understand why they notice, but I don't see the problem! I was so excited about it that I wanted to spend money on it, so of course I want to enjoy it. I'm still in the stage where I catch my reflection and think, heck yeah, excellent purchase. Let me have this. I've never understood buying something I love only to wait and save it for a special day. I know myself. I don't like waiting to enjoy the stuff I buy.
articles.title: 22 Tiny Cats in Tiny Hats I Would Happily Take Fashion Advice From

articles.author: Laurent Shinar
articles.description: Now, in most Cat Distribution System stories our focus is on the feline, their condition and the way in which they are found. And while this story does have those elements it also harbors something far more mystical than even the CDS itself. We begin our tale when our rescuer releases their dogs to play in the yard. Upon which they hear the cries of what they assume to be a bird. But those high pitched wines were not of the aviary kind but from a tiny kitten trapped in a ditch in the neighbor's house. Wasting no time our rescuer got to work and scooped the kitten out of its spot and got it to safety. But not before spending a significant amount of time outdoors with the kitten crying out for its mother. This is a critical step in kitten rescues as often their momma is nearby and very inter…
articles.title: Kitten’s tiny cries save its life when pupper pawrent hears the feline screaming fur its life in CDS delivery

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
Some cats are social butterflies, and others would rather hide under the bed until everyone leaves. They have no interest in making new friends, attending family gatherings, or entertaining unexpected visitors. If they could put a "Do Not Disturb" sign on their favorite hiding spot, we're pretty sure they would.
Can we blame them? As fellow introverts know, socializing can be exhausting. Sometimes you just want to spend the evening curled up somewhere comfortable, enjoying your own company without anyone asking you questions. Cats have been living that dream for centuries, and they don't even have to come up with excuses to cancel plans.
We think introverted cats might actually have the right idea. Why bother making small talk when you could be taking your fourth nap of the afternoon? Why …
articles.title: Introverted Cat Memes That Make Staying Home This Weekend Sound Purrfect

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
Every family has that one dad who insists they're never getting a pet. He doesn't want fur on the furniture, doesn't want another mouth to feed, and definitely doesn't want an animal following him around the house. He's perfectly happy without one, thank you very much. But we've all seen how quickly that attitude can change.
It usually starts with a few complaints. The dog is too loud, the cat is scratching the couch, and somebody needs to explain why there's pet hair on his favorite shirt. Then, slowly, the complaints become less frequent. He starts asking whether the cat has eaten yet. He saves a little space beside him on the couch. Eventually, he's referring to himself as the animal's dad without a hint of irony.
The best part is that these dads rarely admit they've changed their minds…
articles.title: Retired dad who insisted he wasn't a cat person now sends his family daily updates about his new feline friend

articles.author: Celeste Mello
articles.description:
Would Halloween have been half as exciting without the promise of candy?
When I was a kid, Halloween meant it was the time of the year to dress up in a spooky costume and go from house to house with my friends, asking for treats. People usually gave us something, so we got used to the dynamic. We knocked, someone opened the door and filled our pumpkins with candy. Excellent transaction. The best one ever invented. How could we not love Halloween?
I remember one Halloween it rained, and one of my friends' moms drove us around the neighborhood so we could still go trick-or-treating. I remember how happy I was that we didn't have to give up on the evening. We still got to visit houses and collect our treats because she took us. What a generous soul to spend part of her night helping a car full of children get more sugar. I'm still grateful. I hope she's doing well now and all her wishes came true!!
articles.title: A Sweet Stash of Cat Memes Offering a Little Treat Before Halloween

articles.author: Blake Seidel
articles.description:
One thing I never get tired of writing about is how cats somehow find the exact hooman they need, usually in the weirdest way pawssible.
Sometimes, cats show up on a porch and refuse to leave. Other times, they get stuck in a wall, wedged into a car, or trapped somewhere that makes you wonder how they even got there in the first place (the answer is usually magic). There are times when the hooman who helps them cannot keep them furrever, but still takes the time to drive to the vet, make sure they are safe, and foster until they find their forever family. And that, dear readers, is what this week's Caturday Meowgazine is all about.
These 10 stories are all different, but they have one thing in common: somebody noticed. Somebody stopped. Somebody decided that this little life was worth the inconvenience. Comopassion does not care about breed, age, location, or whether the Cat Distribution System completely ruined your plans for the day.
Grab you feline supurrvisor, scroll down, and meet 10 felines whose lives changed because somebody chose to help.
articles.title: Your Weekly Meowgazine of 10 Real Feline Rescue Moments That Prove Compassion Has No Pedigree

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
What would you do if four tiny criminals broke into your car?
We have always said that the cat distribution system works in meowsterious ways, but this one… this was truly spooky. Over my time as a writer here on ICHC, I have seen some strange, strange stories of the CDS in action, so I would like to think that I am somewhat of an expert on the matter. I have purrsonally written about cats following people to their homes when they go on walks. I've covered stories about kittens being handed to people in drive-throughs while they are at work. I have even covered one story about a cat literally flying through someone's window and into their lap and getting adopted. That's how the CDS works. But I have never seen something like this. 
What would you have done if you found out that not one, not two, but four kittens broke into your car? And yes, they are very cute cats. But they are also fierce. They are hardened criminals. They are illegally small. Too tiny for this world but full of criminal thoughts, capable of meownipulation like no one else. There is no one who can say no to a single kitten, let alone four. So, really, the answer to what you would have done is obvious. You would have done whatever they wanted you to do. And if that means adopting them and their mom and then taking care of them all for the rest of their lives, well… they didn't really give you a choice in the matter, did they? It's a good thing that the CDS never gets things wrong anyway, so everyone ends up happy.
articles.title: A fierce gang of four criminals, known as itty bitty kittens, breaks into man's Jeep, forces him to adopt them and then brings them mom to be adopted too

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Saturday mornings are made so much better when they come with a large helping of happy kitties.
As cat pawrents, we know just how good our feline friends have it. They don't know it, but we do. They've never had to fend for themselves on the streets, so they have no idea how lucky they are to have a warm home, a full food bowl, and humans ready to serve them like the meownderful servants that we are. Their fancy food isn't served fast enough? The horror. Their litterbox has a single suspicious clump? Unacceptable. These tiny cute cats act like they have the hardest lives imaginable, and we wouldn't have them any other way. But that's not true for all of them. Newly adopted cats, the ones who have just found their forever homes, they know what they have. 
Newly adopted kitties often appreciate even the tiniest comforts, especially if they've experienced life on the streets. A full food bowl, a cozy bed, a warm lap… It's all cause for celebration. But once they settle in and realize they're finally safe, their true personalities start to shine. The grateful little angels turn into chaotic household rulers, and we somehow fall even harder for them. So, let's kick off our Caturday with a smile and enjoy this week's sweetest cat adoption stories.
articles.title: Meet the Newly Adopted Faces of the Week: 10 Real Stories of Cats Who Finally Found Their Forever Homes (October 24, 2026)

articles.author: Ayala Sorotsky
articles.description:
Meowdern memes have nothing on the classics, and lolcats are the prime example of that nostalgic internet meme culture.
The fact that this week's lolcat batch has exactly 67 memes has made me remember that 6-7 meme. It's really not that long ago that Gen Alpha kids and teens were running amok, yelling "Six seven! Six Seven!" while flailing their arms and laughing as if they'd heard the best joke ever. It was annoying then, and it's annoying now. But then again, it's a little less annoying now… because it's gone. The streets are quiet, no six and no seven, and the kids have moved on to chase other, probably dumber memes.
And that's all there is about the modern meme cycle - it's there for a short period of time, getting its 15 minutes of fame, and then gone as fast as it came. Like a Zippo flame. But that's not how old-school memes work - not just because of nostalgic value, but because they're physically (and metaphorically, in our thoughts) still here. Just take a look at last week's lolcats, and the week before that, and the week before that… And you can trace this line back to the very beginning of them, because the history of lolcats goes that far.
And that's why we have this immense chasm between the memes of yore and the memes of the modern age. They don't last, there's no continuity, and I'm sure there won't be an 8-9 meme to set that flame alight again. It's a Zippo, not a sacred fire burning for decades.
articles.title: Your Weekly Binge of the Best ‘LOLcat’ Cuteness From Cat Meme Lovers Around the World

articles.author: Elna McHilderson
articles.description:
Were cats the original parkour content creators? We're starting to think so…
Have you heard of the thrilling craze of parkour? This is someone who basically ricochets off buildings and other human-made objects found in cities and towns. They bounce around like a ninja in the night. When someone is good at it, it's actually pretty crazy to watch. When someone is bad at it… Well, it's quite literally painful to watch. 
However, it's an amazing spectacle for us humans because the moves you do when parkouring are not natural. They take a lot of training and practice. When a cat moves around as if they practice parkour, it's pretty normal to watch. That's because cats are agile and always land on their feet. It's not crazy to see them bouncing off of one wall, to balancing on a skinny banister, back to another wall, and into your lap like nothing even happened. That's why we say "cat-like reflexes," because they move even better than a parkour professional! 
So when this recently rescued kitten decided to show off his parkour skills right after being rescued from a vent underneath a house, it was a surprise, but not a shock.
articles.title: Stray Kitten Rescued From a Vent Under a House Parkours Into a Car and Wedges Himself Inside the Dashboard, Has to Be Re-Rescued, and Sparks Hilarious Responses From Online Cat Community

articles.author: Cata Holmes
articles.description:
Could your day use a little extra softness?
Have you ever experience that feeling where you don't what to do with the internet? Nowadays, the World Wide Web is full of sad news, conflicts, political news… It's become a source of sadness. Even though it's okay to keep track of what's going on in the world, it can take a toll on us. Sometimes, we just want to get online, look for something cute or fun, and move on with the rest of the day. But it gets complicated when you're stuck with a bunch of news you never meant to see. Being mindful of what you see online takes effort, because it can really affect your mood.
I've been reading about this lately, and many users have confirmed they feel down whenever they go online. And honestly, I agree, since it's happened to me more than I would like. Staying in touch with internet culture and the latest trends takes a lot of time online, but I have one strategy that helps me stay grounded and focused before I get sucked into the bad-news spiral. And that's actually searching for any kind of animal content, whether it's a story about a man and his lion or some good, wholesome cat memes. It always works.
articles.title: 22 Wholesome Cats for a Softer Day on the Internet (October 24, 2026)

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
It's Furiday night, and we're going out! We've spent all week looking forward to seeing our friends, getting out of the house, and having some fun. But as we're getting ready to leave, our cat is sitting by the door, looking suspiciously interested in coming along.
Now, most cats would probably hate the idea of a night out. They're perfectly happy staying home, sleeping on the couch, and enjoying having the entire house to themselves. But some kitties are surprisingly social. They love meeting new people, exploring new places, and getting involved in whatever their humans are doing.
And we have to admit, bringing your cat along on a Furiday night sounds pretty entertaining.
For starters, you'd immediately become the most popular person in your friend group. Nobody would care what you've be…
articles.title: It's Furiday Night And These Cool Cats Are Meowt On The Town

articles.author: Ayala Sorotsky
articles.description:
Cats never miss an opportunity to jump into every space, no matter its size or availability status.
I don't need to iterate on how cats enter every cardboard box they see, or literally any other small space they locate. But first - why do they even do that? In short, cats simply feel safe inside. Having an enclosed space around them, like a cardboard box, gives them a sense of security - however real or not. They also view these spaces as strategic vantage points to pounce on prey from - so basically a place to cosplay big cats. So basically it's just another proof that cats make no sense at all. Their logic is not logicing. But this is why we love them so much.
My cat found herself in the most ridiculous situations because of this internal drive she has to enter literally anywhere. To do the fits and sits even if she doesn't fit and cannot sit. She once got herself stuck behind the washing machine because she absolutely insisted this nook must be explored - she just had no idea how to get herself out. At another time, she got locked inside the pots and pans cabinet, which is protected by a child lock. It was open for one second, and she still managed to get herself inside.
But all of that doesn't make her experience with classic cardboard boxes any easier. That child lock I've mentioned? It's there for a reason. The reason being a 1-year-old roaming free in the house because she's been walking since she was 10 months old. That kid sees the cat entering a cardboard box I left on the floor for her and thinks, "I'm going to get inside to cuddle the cat." My cat bolts away every single time. Raising cats and kids together is not a simple task.
But cats will always cat, and that means they'll fit, sit, and be absolutely smug about it. And honestly? It makes them even more special than they already are.
articles.title: A Box of 23 Cardboard-Loving Cat Memes That Fit & Sit in Your Heart

articles.author: Blake Seidel
articles.description:
What happens when our purrsonal ethics conflict with the biological needs of an animal we chose to care for?
There are a lot of things about cat ownership that become so normal you quickly furrget how objectively weird they are. You scoop their bathroom business into a plastic bag multiple times per day, you spend money on furniture specifically designed to be destroyed, and you quickly learn the difference between their different kinds of meows. One can mean "I'm hungry" and another can mean "I saw a bug a few hours ago and you must know about it." You fellow cat pawrents know what I'm talking about.
And then there is feeding them meat. I don't think anyone likes it. All the wet foods have this weird smell that, even after 12 years of owning cats, I still can't get over. Don't even get me started on the ingredients.
Most longtime cat pawrents probably do not think very deeply about it every time they crack open a can. Cats eat meat, that is simply part of the deal. For one brand-new kitten owner, though, that realization caused something of a moral meat crisis.
They eagerly went out and bought them high-quality kitten food while focusing on giving their baby the best pawssible start. Then, as a strict vegan, they realized that every can of cat food represented an ethical equation they had spent years trying to remove themselves from. Smartly, they did want to force their beliefs onto their kitten, but they also wondered whether there was another way to make it work.
And this is where I think the story gets really interesting, because this is something a lot of vegans deal with. And, we all know that people have a lot of feelings about veganism, whether it's for or against.
articles.title: Strict vegan adopts very first kitten, then realizes that her tiny carnivore needs meat for life, and cat owners have a tough message for her: 'Their wellbeing comes first'

articles.author: Elna McHilderson
articles.description:
You are getting eepy, very eepy. Now, quick, grab your closest feline friend and take a nap! Do you feel better?
Of course you do! There is nothing better than taking a quick snooze with your favorite fur buddy. Not all cats are cuddlers, but all are definitely nappers. Cats can sleep anywhere from 12 to 16 hours a day! Talk about a cat nap… I wonder where that saying came from: "cat nap." Was it something more profound, or was it because humans saw that cats napped all day? Either way, it makes total sense. Cats like to nap! They are the ultimate bestie to get comfy cozy with. Watching a movie on a rainy night? That's pretty good, but now imagine that with a warm, purring kitten on your lap! See? So much better. Just got home from a long, stressful day of work and want to go brain silent for a bit and doomscroll? Well, do that guilt-free when there is a cat by your side just enjoying their cozy time with you. It's different with dogs. Canine companions are great because when you get home, they straight up run laps around the room because they are so happy to see you! But some people aren't at that level of energy, like some cat people. Some pet parents just want to come home and curl up in a blanket and chill. That's purrrrfect for a cozy kitty! And so are these memes.
articles.title: A Cozy Corner of Sleepy Kitty Memes Ready for a Cat Nap

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
With shy cats, patience pays off more than anything else.
We, as humans, have a certain understanding of what love looks like. And whether we do it on purpose or not, we apply that understanding to our cats as well. Now, with dogs, it's simpler. Their way of showing affection is very obvious, it's very in your face. With cats, it's not quite that easy. Some cats are total velcro cats. They are all about physical contact. They will cuddle with you and climb up on you, and if you don't pet them at least 116 times a day, they will riot and directly on your face. But most cats are not like that. 
Cats have their own love language. Cats show affection by slowly blinking at you. They show affection by turning their back on you, by sleeping next to you, by spending long stretches of time in the same room as you. And we know- that's not the same as cuddling your cat. Of course it's not. But their expression of love is no less valid than yours. 
And then, there are shy cats. And shy cats, ones who are a little scared of humans, a little wary of letting their guard down, they show affection in their own ways as well. They do it in small ways, slowly warming up to you. We can't tell you the exact way. It's up to you to pay attention to them and learn how they show love. And you have to appreciate those little things just as much as you would a cuddle session. Maybe once you do that, once they feel comfortable enough with you, they will learn a little about your love language as well.
articles.title: Person adopts the most terrified kitten in the shelter, and after months of careful trustbuilding, she finally lets herself be petted and purrs: '[She was] trying to make herself as small as possible'

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Fall is the purrfect time to sit back with a hot cocoa and soak up the silence. 
Fall is different than summer. And not just in the obvious ways. We're not talking about the cold and the rain and the sweaters and pumpkin spice things, though all of that is nice too. We're talking about the vibes. People are… calmer during fall. Everything is a little bit quieter. Summer is sunny and loud. Fall is generally not. It's cold enough for us to want to walk around wrapped up in blankets, so people don't stay out quite as long, rushing from one indoor place to another. And the ones who do are not stressed from the constant heat, so they are just calmer. And that is purrfect. It's why fall is the best season, and I will fight on this hill. 
Fall is the purrfect time to soak up the silence. With the rain gently tapping the window, with everything a little bit colder, a little bit slower, but not quite so cold and slow that it's unbearable, it's a good time to paws and enjoy the meowment. Breathe in deep, ignore the chaos of social media, and go home, cuddle with your cat. 
For me, there is not much that can make this time of year better. My cat is cuddly as heck, the fluffy blankets are so fluffy, and the rainy weather is always strangely calming. Throwing in a couple of good cat memes never hurts though. It can only make things better. So, here they are, the peaceful but silly cat memes that I've chosen for today - the purrfect addition to an already lovely day, and the best substitute for doomscrolling on your social media.
articles.title: 25 Peaceful Cat Memes of Sunbeam Soaking and Purrfect Serenity

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
Getting a second cat is always a bit of a gamble. You hope your resident kitty will be thrilled to have a new friend, but there's also the possibility they'll spend the next six months hissing at each other from opposite ends of the couch. Some cats love having company, while others seem purrsonally offended that you've brought another animal into their home without consulting them first.
When two cats really hit it off, though, it's hard to beat watching their friendship develop. One day they're cautiously sniffing each other, and a few weeks later, they're grooming each other's faces and refusing to sleep separately. You'll buy them two perfectly good cat beds, only to find both cats squeezed into the same one. Apparently, having a best friend means never having to respect personal space…
articles.title: Woman worries her cat won't accept his new kitten sister until she catches them cuddling in the cutest way

articles.author: Briana Viser
articles.description:
How we begin our morning may dictate how the rest of the day goes, so starting on the right paw with these friendly cat memes may just do the trick!
Being a cat pawrent can be summed up pretty easily. 
You wake up a pink nose in your face, the breath of a cat's mouth inhaling and exhaling right on top of you, and a few licks to your cheeks before you pull yourself from the sweet slumber you were in to feed this hungry kitty. You wake up to the cheer, smile, and morning barks of joy from your little one. They may not always seem like it but they're full of friendly friendship despite their chaotic appearance and behavior. 
One second they're peacefully napping, paws twitching in dreamland, and the next, they're sitting upright and giving you a look that makes you question whether you're safe to fall asleep tonight. Their eyes are shining in hope that you'll give them what they want. And if they hear the crinkle of the treat bag, be prepared to give them something, because they won't stop until they have it. They might even sneak up behind you for something you're already eating, as we all know the hungry appetite of a cat. Heaven forbid you sit down for a bite without inviting them, or giving them a piece of what you're eating. They will throw their paws right on the table if they have to just for a bit of your bite. And there you have it! The world of cat pawrenting. But never fear, because all the hostility is simply on the surface of what's actually going on, and what's underneath is furry friendship, and cats that embrace feline friendliness. 
We all need a friend in the world, and cats are no different. So if you're wondering why your cat acts so hot and cold to you, remember that they indeed love and need you, but they sometimes need to give the cold shoulder too. At the end of the day, they're still cats. And their love is expressed through the looks of anger, terror, or mischief.
articles.title: 20 Cats Being Furry Friends and Embracing Feline Friendliness

articles.author: Giuliana Tiscioni
articles.description:
Have you ever had a cat with attachment issues? Cats are not usually very clingy, but sometimes they choose their hoomans as their safe space. 
When an animal has been abandoned, it's usual for them to have trust issues in relation to human beings. After all, they were the ones who abandoned them in the first place. Both cats and dogs alike can be scared, reluctant to trust and jumpy before any kind of strange noise. 
I've seen rescued cats and dogs behaving in the same way. The first week my kitty was at home after she was rescued, she was terrified. She opened her eyes round and wide as two full moons; her ears were always up, and she turned her head form one side to the other. All she did was cuddle in the couch and sleep, and every time someone made the smallest of noises, she would run away and hide under the couch. We couldn't even open the front door without her getting scared and hiding. It took her a few weeks to get used to the sounds of the house, and even months to start trusting us an behaving like a regular cat. She wouldn't meow at first either! She was so silent, as if she was afraid thta, if we noticed she was there, we would hurt her. It breaks my heart to remember it, but luckily, now she's all better. 
Now, she meows normally, although she's not the most talkative. She always gets the zoomies, and plays around the house. She's even starting to misbehave! Now, I can't stop her from scratching the furniture or jumping all over the dining table. Seriously, if anyone has the number of a good cat trainer, please, send it to me. I'm getting desperate, and now I can't get her to quit her bad habits. 
In this case, this couple rescued a girl cat who was terrified, and in bringing her to their home, she chose the woman as her source of protection. Now, she won't leave her alone, and she follows her everywhere.
articles.title: Couple rescues terrified kitten from neighboring building, and she attaches herself to the woman asking for constant cuddles and uppies: ‘She trusts me 100%’

articles.author: Ayala Sorotsky
articles.description:
Watching the Cat Distribution System work its magic is like looking at the most heartwarming magic show in the world.
Nobody knows how the Cat Distribution System actually works. Not even we here at the I Can Has Cheezburger HQ. But they (it?) have three parts to their name, so I'll try my best to explore and explain what the CDS actually is in three parts - just like the three cats it sent to this one woman below.
Firstly, cat. When you talk about the CDS, you talk about cats. There are plenty of cats in need out there on the streets - some are hungry, others are suffering extreme weather conditions, and other cats deal with all of these while also giving birth to kittens outside. That's a crazy thought to hold, especially if you're a cat lover. For me at least, it's hard thinking there are cats outside right now that might need help that I can't give them at the moment. It breaks my heart a little.
Secondly, distribution. The CDS doesn't just deal with cats - it sends them where they need to go. Or, you know, it distributes them. Somewhere out there, there's a human who will give a cat a forever home, and that might just be this specific human and that specific cat. And that distribution part is what makes this matchmaking take place. But how do they know to match the right cat to the right person, and vice versa?
That's where the third part comes in, the system. It's not random, despite it being seen as such. Take this one woman who tells her CDS story below - it seems like such a coincidence that she'd be chosen for a match three times, but that's not a random chance at all. This is the CDS at work. You see, she already had five cats, which immediately flagged her as a safe space for cats on the CDS side. They didn't wander into her yard "just because" - they went there to meet their forever home. It's exactly where and when they should've been.
articles.title: ‘The Cat Distribution System chose my yard 3 times’: Woman’s five-cat household grows to eight over two years, and every new arrival opens the family's heart a little more

articles.author: Ayala Sorotsky
articles.description:
Some cats are just wilder than others.
There are cats who can sit on your lap all day long, only taking food and bathroom breaks because they have to - and then returning to steal some more of your body warmth (and your heart). But then there are the absolute demons, the spawns of satan who were probably pspspsed here during a dark summoning ritual. My cat is not like that. Sure, she has the occasional zoomies trip in the middle of the night, but she's not the complete ruckus mess some other cats are. My friend's cat, though… he's another story completely.
Way before I had a cat of my own, I took a vacation for a month, and it just so happened that this friend needed a place to stay. I sublet my room to her and her cat. She warned me he's a wacky one, and this wasn't news - I already heard the stories about him directly from her. The Prophet was his name. Well, Elijah initially, but the more character he's shown as he grew up, the more it became clear he needed his own title. So… Elijah The Prophet, yes? He's an absolute maniac.
When I came back home after the sublet/vacation period, I returned to a room I did not recognize. The curtains were rolled up above the window, the computer was on the highest shelf of my closet (yes, inside), and the office chair was shredded to pieces. That was the art exhibition The Prophet left me. Or, more accurately, his hooman. The chair thing was inevitable, but the curtains and my PC were thoughtfully well-defended. But with that being said, I don't think I'm about to host that crazy cat in my house ever again. At least the story I was left with is funny, as are all this cat's other stories.
articles.title: 31 Feline Funnies for People Raising Ruckus Cat Children

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Rehoming a cat, sometimes, is the kindest choice. 
Generally, of course, we are against cats being rehomed. There are so many solutions to so many issues that can be found. Letting your cat go should always be the last choice. Because as smart as cats are, they are still just cats, and they don't understand rehoming. They just think that they were abandoned by their owners. But sometimes, when the problem is insurmountable, surrendering your cat is not only the right choice, it's also the kindest one. 
We always say that people should adopt a cat when they are ready, when they have enough stability in their lives. If that stability is gone, and if it can't be brought back, then you should not have a cat. It's simple to understand, but it's not easy to do. Of course, people do it all the time. We could write stories about abandoned cats every day, and we wouldn't run out. The only thing that we ask is that if you have to do it, do it right. Don't throw your indoor cat onto the street to fend for themselves. Find them another home if you can, and if you can't, take them to a shelter. So that they have an actual chance to be found by a new person who will love them just as much as you did. Like the person in today's story loves this cat.
articles.title: 'To the person who loved my cat before': Person writes a heartfelt letter to their cat's previous owner who loved the cat but had to let him go to a new home

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Each cat has their own unique and ever so slightly hilarious way of showing affection. 
I did not grow up with cats. Despite that, I thought that I knew cats. I always loved them. Pspspsing cute stray cats was one of my favorite activities forever and always. And I did know a lot. But not everything. Of course, a bunch of things ended up surprising me. The fact that cats have purrsonalities - like, the fact that they are really opinionated and like making sure that we know their opinions. The fact that cats are smart - that they learn our patterns and use that knowledge against us all the time. And the fact that they even though cats hate vet visits, they love giving us heart attacks sometimes and forcing us to take them. 
But one thing about cats that I thought was obvious that ended up taking me by surprise is that cats show affection in all kinds of silly ways. I knew about the meaning of slow blinking, and I knew that if a cat comes to cuddle you, that's basically a declaration of love. I did not know that them showing you their bootie is a sign of affection. I didn't know that my cat sleeping by my feet in bed is them showing love. For my cat specifically, I didn't know that her running to greet me when I come home is a way of showing affection until I realized that she only does it for me and no one else. And for Rotisserie Chicken - the kitty in today's story… showing love means being a rotisserie chicken.
articles.title: Kind person adopts their friend's cat after they suddenly pass, and finds out the cat asks to be held in the silliest way: 'Rotisserie Chicken has learned that he needs a box he can't fit in to communicate he wants to be held'

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
We have a theory that everyone is secretly a cat person. Some people just haven't met the right cat yet. You can spend your entire life insisting you're a dog person, but all it takes is one adorable little face to make you reconsider everything you thought you knew about yourself.
Of course, we understand why some people are hesitant around cats. Unlike dogs, who tend to make their feelings pretty obvious, cats can be a little harder to read. One minute they're rubbing against your legs, and the next they're looking at you like you've committed some terrible offense. Their affection often comes on their own terms, and earning their trust can take a little patience.
But that's also part of what makes getting close to a cat so rewarding. The first time a shy kitty approaches you for attenti…
articles.title: Lifelong dog person never imagined becoming a cat lover until one frightened shelter kitty stole their heart

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
If you think your conversations at home are private, you clearly don't have a cat. These nosy little creatures have a habit of appearing whenever something interesting is happening, especially when it doesn't involve them. Whether you're gossiping with a friend or having a serious conversation, there's a good chance your feline roommate is listening.
Cats are naturally curious animals, and they seem particularly interested in whatever their humans are doing. You could spend hours trying to get your kitty's attention, only for them to suddenly become fascinated by you the moment you pick up the phone. Hearing one side of a conversation is far more entertaining than playing with the expensive toys you bought them.
Some cats aren't particularly subtle about their eavesdropping, either. They'l…
articles.title: Purrivate Conversations Are Impossible With These Nosy Cats Hiding Around Corners To Eavesdrop

articles.author: Celeste Mello
articles.description:
Would you give a band a chance just because every member was a cat?
I absolutely would. I'm in a neo-soul band, but unfortunately, none of us are cats. That would have been hilarious. In fact, we tried to make our bassist's cat part of the band, but his cat wasn't so interested. He ran away during every practice session and only came back for the food.
For a big part of my life, I enjoyed music as a listener. I grew up listening to other people's songs. I went through a pop era that revolved around Justin Bieber, a punk era led by Green Day, an alternative rock era with The Strokes and Arctic Monkeys, and an emo era with My Chemical Romance. These days, I'm also a Swiftie. As you can see, my playlists have been through a lot. But I hadn't made my own music until I started playing drums and joined a band in 2021. Becoming friends with my bandmates and making songs together changed my relationship with music. So for about five years now, we've been creating our own songs, which has given me another way to enjoy music. I can try cool grooves with my friends and help turn something we're playing around with into something interesting.
Musicians know that listening to your finished album is one of the most satisfactory experiences. We finally have the recorded result of all that time we spent making music together, recording, editing, producing... So after years of getting attached to other people's songs, it's nice to think that someone might discover ours and connect with them too.
articles.title: 20 Cats With Musical Instruments Looking Like They’re About to Drop the Album of the Year

articles.author: Cata Holmes
articles.description:
Who needs scary monsters when you've got your cat dressed as one?
Why do we love dressing up our cats? It's a crazy thing to think about, since most cats don't like being touched or put in clothes. But there's something so cute about it that literally melts everyone's hearts. The most adorable part is that every cat looks so cute and tiny in those little clothes that fit them perfectly. Just look at the pictures I gathered below, and you'll see what I mean; it'll be impossible not to consider dressing your cat in any of these costumes this Halloween.
Cat costumes don't have to be elaborate or complicated. You can put them in a little vinnie, a hat, or some booties, and they'll be ready to go trick-or-treating with you. But it's important that you consider their safety and happiness before your own desires. Because if it were up to us, we'd dress up our pets every day, not just on Halloween, but if you know your feline isn't a fan of clothes and doesn't really like being touched or held… maybe that isn't an option this year. That's a boomer…
The good thing is that, for some reason, there're multiple cats out there that actually enjoy wearing costumes and look happy in the ones they got this year. So, for the rest of us humans who don't own a cat or really don't know any cat who likes to wear clothes, we can have a wonderful time looking at this gallery. I'm already excited to see more ideas like this!
articles.title: 'Happy Meowloween!': 22 Cats in Halloween Costumes Ready for a Spooktacular Party

articles.author: Celeste Mello
articles.description:
What is it about a tiny kitten that makes adults forget how to have a normal conversation? Why am I using my baby voice again?
I can be talking about work or explaining something from class sounding like a true professional. When a kitten appears, I forget how grown-ups talk. Hiii, baby! Who's a little baby? The kitten is just sitting there while I'm asking him silly questions about why their face is so small. 
I do this with cat pictures, too. I can be looking at my phone and say, "Oh, look at you!" out loud while scrolling through Instagram reels. Even though there's no cat actually there to receive the compliment. It can be a stranger's kitten, but he showed up in my feed, so he's getting my compliment. He will never know this, but I don't care. He's completely unaware that I love his cute little eyes.
You know that baby voice we use with our pets? Sometimes we don't even realize we've switched. Well, researchers studied it. A 2022 study found that people speak at a higher pitch when addressing cats than when talking to adults. It's called cat-directed speech. So yes, the voice I hope nobody overhears has a name and a study. 
And don't you feel your cat notices when you speak to them and not to someone else? That is actually real. Cats can pick up on the difference. In a small study involving 16 cats, researchers played recordings of their owners and strangers speaking. The cats distinguished between speech addressed to them and speech addressed to adults when their owner was talking, but didn't show that distinction with strangers. Isn't that sweet? Your voice means something to your cat.
articles.title: Your Weekly Delivery of 25 Soft and Silly Kitten Memes for a Midweek Mood Boost (October 21, 2026)

articles.author: Ayala Sorotsky
articles.description:
Cat person or not, seeing stray cats in need always moves something in people's hearts.
I was not always a cat person, but that changed when I started living with a cat. The cat was not mine, he officially belonged to a roommate I lived with when I was a student. This is the cat that made me warm up to cats, the previously self-described "dog person, but cats are also okay I guess". It made me love cats so much that I adopted my own cat, my beloved Cassie, whom I held in my arms for the first time when she was a month-old kitten. She's seven now, and the queen of my heart.
But that's the meowgical power of cats over people. They might not be "cat people" like us - dedicated fans and feline fanatics - but their hearts are opening up to the possibility. And that's how cat people are made, just by being around cats, learning to live by their side, or seeing that they're in need. This latter option is what this one woman experienced and shared with the broader online feline family - she was not a cat person. But one mama cat and her two kittens lived outside her house for a few months, in the grueling heat, in need to be homed.
It's a psychological phenomenon that works between humans too. It's called "the helper's high", and it basically describes the release of oxytocin (the bonding hormone) in our brains when we engage in prosocial behavior. That's the "high" we experience when we want to help someone, and definitely when we do help someone. And that someone can be a cat… or a cat mama and her kittens, living outside your house. And with this phenomenon, it really isn't that surprising that more people than not are becoming cat people.
articles.title: Neighbor who never saw herself as a cat person catches a mama cat and her two kittens after several months of watching them roam the block: ‘You saved 3 lives.’

articles.author: Mariel Ruvinsky
articles.description:
Cat memes are the purrfect sweetener to add into your hot cup of coffee.
There are three things that I need to start my morning on the right paw. They are simple. The first one is a kiss on my cat's forehead. I must have that. If I don't… morning ruined. The second thing is my coffee. And I'm very specific about how I make it. If my husband gets it wrong… morning ruined. But the third thing is what really makes a difference, and sometimes I don't quite follow through with this thing. Who has the time in the morning, when you're rushing to get ready for work, to scroll through cute cat pictures or funny cat memes? No one, right? Well, I have to. Because if not, then my morning is ruined. 
Because you know what? If I don't scroll through wholesome cat content that makes me smile, I scroll through something else. I get on social media, and I scroll away, and all I get with my morning coffee is bitterness and salt. Because that is what social media is right meow. I'll see the occasional viral cat thing, but for the most part, my timeline is filled with things that are not quite that sweet. That's where cat memes come in. It's where ICHC comes in. You think that just because I write on this site means that I don't use it in my daily life? It's the opposite. It's exactly why I use it. Because I know what we put up here. I know that our content is here to make people smile and help them get their mornings right.
articles.title: 25 Cat Coffee Memes to Pour a Little Laughter Into Your Cozy Cup

articles.author: Giuliana Tiscioni
articles.description:
Have you ever tried to introduce a new cat to your current cat? 
Well, I've tried, and let me tell you, it's not as easy as people think. At first, you're so excited because you think, "My furbaby won't be alone anymore when I go to work; he'll have a companion!" But then you realize it's not all rosy in the garden. 
You see, cats are very territorial animals, whether in the wild or as one of our fluffy pets. They consider their territory their own, and they can feel threatened and feel the need to protect and defend it if another cat trespasses. Granted, not all cats are so dramatic, especially not domestic ones. In my experience, most of the time they'll just be annoyed and indifferent to the new cat for a while. Then they just start tolerating each other while pretending the other one doesn't exist. Basically, that's what I did in high school with my classmates. No wonder my boyfriend says I have the purrsonality of a cat. 
Either way, what happened with my cats was something along those lines. For context, my grandmother and I live next to each other, and she has a cat who loved coming to visit. She would eat here, sleep in my bed, walk around and explore the whole place, and basically treat my house as her own. But then, one day, I brought home my current cat. It was all from one day to the next, so there was no time to try an adaptation process. My grandma's cat was not happy. She didn't attack or anything; she's not aggressive, but she refuses to come inside my house now and hisses every time she sees my cat. I'm a little sad about it, but I still get to see her when walking in the yard, when I go to Grandma's house, and I know she's well taken care of. 
In this case, we have an orange furball named Copper, who suddenly got an unexpected companion. Let's just say it'll take a while for him to process everything.
articles.title: Two wholesome orange fluffy felines have a meet-cute worthy on an enemies-to-lovers movie: ‘Copper was not a fan of the new girl’

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
Going for a walk is supposed to be pretty straightforward. You put on your shoes, head outside, get some fresh air, and eventually make your way home. But sometimes a neighborhood cat decides to join you, and suddenly your peaceful evening stroll involves making a new furry friend who has no intention of leaving your side.
Cats aren't usually the first animals we think of as walking companions, but some are enthusiastic about tagging along. They'll trot beside you, weave between your legs, and stop to make sure you're still paying attention. You might even find yourself slowing down because your new friend insists on investigating every bush along the way.
We wonder what makes certain cats so comfortable approaching strangers. Maybe they're naturally outgoing, or perhaps they've learned th…
articles.title: Couple thinks they've said goodbye to a stray cat until he comes racing back to them the next evening

articles.author: Sarah Brown
articles.description:
Who needs a life coach when you've got a cat at home? These furry little philosophers seem to have everything figured out, from getting enough sleep to convincing someone else to pay all their bills. Their advice might be questionable, but they've certainly mastered the art of living comfortably.
Cats have some pretty interesting ideas about how hoomans should live. For starters, they firmly believe that getting enough sleep should be everyone's top priority. Feeling stressed? Take a nap. Have a deadline approaching? Take another nap. Someone needs you to do something important? Pretend you didn't hear them and go back to sleep. We could probably benefit from adopting at least a little of that attitude.
They've also mastered the art of setting boundaries. Cats have absolutely no problem wa…
articles.title: Wise Cat Memes With Life Lessons Nobody Asked For but Everyone Needs

articles.author: Blake Seidel
articles.description:
When a cat adopts you, resistance is futile. Especially if it's a gigantic orange cat that bites French people.
I have mixed feelings about cat cafés. On the one hand, I love having a place outside my own home where I can be surrounded by cats, and on the other hand, I feel bad for them.
The good news is that cat cafés have improved a lot in the last couple of years. When they first started, they were basically a petting zoo for cats. No one really cared for the cats' needs, as they were merely a means to bring customers into the café. Now, the purpose of most of these cafés is for cat adoption instead of being entertainment for people while they dine or sip on a cup of mediocre coffee. Of course, there are still some cafés that use them as a tool, so always do your research before visiting a cat (or any animal) café. 
Sometimes, people go there for the purrpose of finding a cat to adopt, while others, like the visitor in our "story" today from Japan, actually end up getting adopted. Simply coming in for a cup of coffee, they were warned about a purrmanently grumpy orange cat who had serious cattitude. He was notorious for knocking drinks off of tables and apparently biting French people. How he knew they were French, we have no idea, but apparently, he knew.
After a fair amount of warning, the menacing ginger cat actually climbed into their lap and started purring. Needless to say, the staff were shocked. They demanded the visitor take him home, even to the point of practically shoving adoption papers into their hands before leaving. 
Even if this story is a well-written joke, there's still a lesson in there that we could all take home with us: don't judge cats by their appearances. Some of the "grumpiest" cats I've ever met have been the biggest snuggle bugs as soon as they meet their purrson and find a place they finally feel safe. And, as always, when a cat chooses you, your fate has already been decided for you. That's just the way the Cat Distribution System works.
articles.title: Giant ginger cat built like a retired wrestler rules over Japanese cat café with an iron paw, until one visitor who just came in for coffee wins his heart and gets handed adoption papers
